name: frame_survey
description: Look at EVERY frame of a video: numbered contact sheets with the frame number and time on each tile, a change score that makes a short run of differing frames stand out without a scene cut, a range of frames at native size, and a checked repair of an MP4 or AVI that will not open. THE DECODER is ffmpeg (5.1 or later for -fps_mode; an older one is given -vsync 0), with ffprobe for the stream's shape, run as programs: this tool has no decoder of its own, and where ffmpeg or ffprobe is not on PATH every mode answers status failed with that reason in one JSON document (repair still prints the container's diagnosis, which needs no decoder). RULES (they are in every answer and in every refusal too): (1) Survey first, with the default call ({"video": ...}): every frame is decoded, tiled with its frame number and time, and scored. Read `runs` before the sheets: a run is a stretch of frames in which one region changed and changed back (a caption, an overlay, a flash) with no scene cut, and it names the sheets that show it. (2) A sampled or capped survey is `partial` and says what it skipped (every, max_frames, the clock): a run shorter than the sampling step can fall between two samples, so "nothing stands out" is a negative only for a `complete` survey with every: 1. (3) Take the frames a run names at native size ({"mode": "extract", "first": N, "last": M}) before reading text off a tile: a tile is a reduced copy. Frame numbers count decoded frames of the first video stream from 0; a time is the frame's own presentation time when the decoder gave one, else frame / rate, and the answer says which. (4) A file that will not open goes to {"mode": "repair"}: it says what the container lacks (an MP4's moov, a cut mdat, an AVI's index), writes a remuxed copy, and counts the frames that copy DECODES. The count decoded is the claim; a missing moov with no second file from the same recorder is not rebuilt, and the answer says so. SURVEY (the default): the first video stream is decoded once, each frame reduced to a tile (tile_width, default 160) on a pipe; a tile keeps the frame's shape up to twice as high as wide, and a taller frame is fitted into that box (tile_keeps_shape false, tile_note says how it was stretched); a sheet whose pixels would pass 192 MiB is refused (ask fewer columns or rows); tiles go left to right, top to bottom, columns x rows a sheet (default 10 x 6), on sheet-0001.png onward, each with its frame number and time (a 3 x 5 pixel font of the tool's own); frames.tsv has one row a decoded frame (frame, time, where the time came from, score) and windows.tsv one a window. THE SCORE of a frame is the share of 32 x 18 blocks whose mean moved by more than 8 of 255 from the frame decoded before it: a scene cut changes half of the blocks or more at once (scene_cuts); a local change (a caption, an overlay, a flash, an object entering) changes few. A RUN is a pair of local changes over the same region with no cut between them, the first when the region changed and the second when it changed again: first_frame to last_frame, the region in native pixels and the sheets that show it. It is a candidate, from block means alone: steady motion in one region, or noise above the step, can make one, and a change that covers half the picture is a cut, not a run; what a run shows is read from the frames (extract). A local change is paired with the first matching one among the next 400 local changes, within 2,000 decoded frames; one without a partner is listed apart, and the pairing has 10 seconds of its own (past them the answer is partial and says from which frame). windows_that_stand_out ranks windows (window frames each, default 10) by their highest score against the clip's own median. every: N samples one frame in N and max_frames (default 20000) caps the frames decoded; either makes the answer partial with skipped and, for a cap or the clock, the start_frame to go on from (the cap is reached only when a frame past it comes: a stream of exactly max_frames frames is whole). FRAME NUMBERS: the decoder is run with one set of filters for the whole stream (-reinit_filter 0), so that a stream that changes size or format mid-way does not start again the count the frames are picked by; the times and sizes are matched to frames in the order the decoder gives them. A rebuild of the filters it makes anyway (its own line, or a counter that is not the one after the last) is counted: extract then keeps no frame given after it (their files are removed, the answer is partial, and failed when none is left), and a survey that started late or sampled is partial from that frame on (numbers_unconfirmed_from). EXTRACT: frames first to last (at most 300 a call) at native size as PNG, each with its sha256 and time. Each frame's size is confirmed by the decoder's own line: a frame decoded at another size than the stream's (a stream that changes size) is scaled to it, marked native: false with its decoded_size, and makes the answer partial; frames are never cut out of the decoder's output at a size it did not give. ROTATION: a display rotation by a quarter or half turn is applied by the decoder, which moves pixels without resampling them: every size, frame and region is then of the turned frame, as a player shows it, and rotation_note gives the angle and the coded size; another angle is not applied (it would resample) and rotation_note says so. A display matrix that mirrors the picture (ffprobe gives a horizontal mirror as a rotation of 180 degrees) is applied with the turn, and rotation_note says the picture is mirrored. A file with more than one video stream: only the first is read, and streams_note says so. TIMES: the frame's own presentation time, read from the decoder's showinfo line, when the decoder gave one, else frame / rate; times says how many of each. REPAIR: the container is read first, without a decoder (an MP4's top-level boxes: moov missing, moov at end, a box cut by the end of the file, fragments; an AVI's chunks: the RIFF or movi list cut, idx1 missing or broken), then ffmpeg remuxes what its demuxer reads (streams copied, no frame re-encoded; an MP4 with its moov in front, an AVI with a new index) into repaired.mp4 or repaired.avi, and the copy's first video stream is decoded to nothing and its frames counted. rebuilt and could_not say what was and was not rewritten; claim gives the two counts (the original's and the copy's); the count decoded is all that is verified, not that the frames are the scene's, in order, or all there were. A file with no moov box is NOT rebuilt (its sample tables and codec configuration are not in it, and no reference-file repair is run): failed, with could_not. A copy that decodes no frame is failed, never a repair. Files go to a new directory under $OUT (outside a job, under work/<AGENT_ID>/tool-output; an AGENT_ID that is not a plain name is refused); the repaired copy is written there by ffmpeg itself, the sheets and frames by this tool. Status: complete when the decoder ended cleanly at the end of the stream and every frame it gave was tiled and scored (the container's own frame count is printed beside the decoder's; the decoder's is what was read); partial for a sample, a cap, the clock, a damaged stream (a non-zero exit code, or any line the decoder wrote about an error, a corrupt or missing packet or a concealed frame while it decoded, whatever its exit code, the input's own name taken out of the line before it is judged: decoder_said has the first three; a demuxer's word on a cut file, such as Matroska's "File ended prematurely", is such a line), a whole-stream survey that decodes fewer frames than the container lists, or whose last frame falls short of the duration the container states by more than two frames (a container with no frame count, such as Matroska, WebM or a bare stream, is held to its duration; a video stream that ends before the file's other streams is partial for the same reason), frames decoded at another size than the stream's (frames_of_another_size), a decoder that ended while a process it left held its pipe (read for at most 1 MiB and 1 second more; the frames read after it ended are counted in the reason), or a file that could not be written; every count of what was not read or not judged is printed in not_read_or_judged (zeros included), and the status is derived from that one list: any count above zero is partial (frames without the decoder's own showinfo line among them: a decoder log line longer than 64 KiB, such as a long metadata value, is read in pieces and judged whole, decoder_log says how many there were); a program that left a process behind makes it partial too (program_group; on a host that cannot adopt orphans, such as macOS, every call that ran the decoder is partial for that reason alone). Bounds: frames of up to 8192 wide and 4320 high as coded (each side, read from the stream's header; a frame turned by its display rotation is turned after), and every frame the decoder meets at most 8192 x 4320 pixels in all (its -max_pixels: a larger frame later in the stream is not decoded, and its error makes the answer partial), 200,000 frames a call, a tile of at most 480 x 960, the clock (max_seconds, default 500, at most 540; the manifest's timeout is 600, and what may follow the clock, the 20 seconds below, the pairing's 10 and the decoder's ending, stays under it) read for every frame; a picture whose encoding began before the clock ran out is given 20 seconds more, past which it is not written and the answer says so. A whole number out of its range is refused with that parameter's own range. Measured with Python 3.12 and ffmpeg 9.0 on an Apple M-series host: a 320 x 180 MPEG-4 clip of 150 frames surveyed in 0.4 s; 3,000 frames of 1280 x 720 H.264 in 4.1 s (about 730 frames a second, 50 sheets); a job VM may be several times slower. A NAME with a printf pattern and a picture extension (x%03d.png) is the one file it names: ffprobe and the decoder read it with -pattern_type none, never as a numbered sequence of other files, and repair refuses such a name (copy the file under another name). ffprobe is asked for the fields read here only (no stream tags but rotate). Paths are printed as given; the decoder's own error lines are printed (they can quote a stream's metadata). A stop signal ends it with one JSON answer (failed, interrupted), exit 128 + the signal; the decoder is ended with it and a file that was begun is removed.

mode.description: survey (default: contact sheets and change scores), extract (frames first to last at native size) or repair (diagnose the container, write a remuxed copy, count the frames it decodes)

every.description: survey: decode one frame in this many (default 1: every frame). More than 1 makes the answer partial: a run shorter than this can fall between two samples

start_frame.description: survey: begin at this frame number (default 0); use the number a capped or clock-limited answer names to go on

max_frames.description: survey: the most frames decoded in this call (default 20000, at most 200000); a cap that is reached (a frame past it comes) makes the answer partial

tile_width.description: survey: the width of a tile in pixels (default 160, 64 to 480); the height keeps the frame's shape up to twice the width, and a taller frame is fitted into that box

columns.description: survey: tiles in a row of a sheet (default 10, 1 to 20)

rows.description: survey: rows of a sheet (default 6, 1 to 20)

window.description: survey: frames in one window of windows.tsv (default 10, 2 to 1000)

first.description: extract: the first frame number to write

last.description: extract: the last frame number to write (default: first; at most 300 frames a call)

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 500, 5 to 540; the manifest's timeout is 600)
